nodes.name: AEMWE Stack Assembly
nodes.procedure: A detailed material analysis was featured in previous work [10], and here a 5-cell, 500 cm² non-PGM AEMWE stack was created with the same materials and evaluated under galvanostatic operation. The stack incorporates a patent-pending two-phase flow field and a consistent membrane-electrode assembly (Ni Fiber-Raney Ni ∥ X37-50RT ∥ NiFeOx-SS316L fiber).
nodes.source_text: A detailed material analysis was featured in previous work,[10] and here a 5-cell, 500 cm² non-PGM AEMWE stack was created with the same materials... incorporating a patent-pending two-phase flow field and a consistent membrane-electrode assembly (Ni Fiber-Raney Ni ∥ X37-50RT ∥ NiFeOx-SS316L fiber)

nodes.description: AEMWE stack performance characterization across 5 cells at multiple current densities
nodes.source_text: Figure 1a shows the linear sweep voltammogram (LSV) for the five cells, where all cells maintain approximately 1.0 Acm⁻² at 2.0 V... HHV-based efficiency at 1.0 Acm⁻² (2.0 V) is 74.1% which translates to an energy consumption of approximately 53.2 kWh kg_H2⁻¹... series resistance decreases by 34.6% from an average of 139 mΩ cm⁻² at 0.2 Acm⁻² to 91 mΩ cm⁻² at 1.0 Acm⁻². In contrast, the polarization resistance reduces 79.2% from 396.85 mΩ cm⁻² to 82.87 mΩ cm⁻².

nodes.description: OER charge transfer characterization via DRT analysis in stack

observation.value: P4O2 dominant at high current densities, rate-limiting

nodes.source_text: The second peak around 900 Hz is dominated by OER charge transfer... The P4 peak, observed around 208.78 Hz at 0.2 Acm⁻², shifts to 305.42 Hz at 0.5 Acm⁻² and vanishes by 1.0 Acm⁻²... the P5 peak shifts from 886.07 to 1296.19 Hz while steadily decreasing in magnitude.

nodes.description: Membrane performance in AEMWE stack - ion transport analysis

observation.value: no clear high-frequency PS peak for OH⁻ ion transport

nodes.source_text: The absence of the typical high-frequency PS peak attributed to OH⁻ ion transport between HER and the OER regions suggests that this process is either suppressed or obscured in the stack environment.

nodes.characterization_summary: Linear sweep voltammogram shows all five cells maintain approximately 1.0 A cm⁻² at 2.0 V with homogeneous performance.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1a shows the linear sweep voltammogram (LSV) for the five cells, where all cells maintain approximately 1.0 A cm⁻² at 2.0 V.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS Nyquist plots show uniform semicircular profiles across cells at 0.2, 0.5, and 1.0 A cm⁻²; series resistance decreases 34.6% from 139 mΩ cm⁻² to 91 mΩ cm⁻², polarization resistance reduces 79.2% from 396.85 mΩ cm⁻² to 82.87 mΩ cm⁻² due to Joule heating and enhanced kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EIS spectra in Figure 2a demonstrate uniform polarization impedances across the five-cell AEMWE stack, with Nyquist plots revealing a consistent semicircular profile... The series resistance decreases by 34.6% from an average of 139 mΩ cm⁻² at 0.2 A cm⁻² to 91 mΩ cm⁻² at 1.0 A cm⁻².

nodes.characterization_summary: DRT analysis reveals peaks at ~208 Hz (P4H₂, HER charge transfer) and ~900 Hz (P4O₂, OER charge transfer) that decrease in magnitude and shift to higher frequencies with increasing current density; shoulder peak P3 (40-80 Hz, gas/water diffusion) disappears at higher currents.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The DRT analysis of the stack in Figure 2c reveals several distinct features... The first prominent peak, at approximately 208 Hz, is primarily attributed to charge transfer of the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER).
